skill.name: firebase

finding_verdicts.reason: The snippet is a React path template literal passed to useDocument. It is documentation code and does not execute a shell command.

content.value_statement: Firebase projects can become expensive or insecure when data models, rules, and auth flows are improvised. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for Firebase architecture, rules, auth, functions, hosting, and cost-aware design.
actual_capabilities: Shows modular Firebase SDK imports and Firestore read, query, and listener patterns.
Provides Firestore security rule examples for owners, admins, public data, and private subcollections.
Explains data modeling choices for denormalized, query-first Firestore schemas.
Outlines Cloud Functions v2 patterns for HTTP APIs, triggers, schedules, and cleanup tasks.
Covers Firebase Auth flows including social login, account linking, persistence, verification, password reset, and token handling.
Lists related tools for rules testing, emulators, React, Vue, and Angular integrations.
limitations: It does not deploy projects or access a Firebase account by itself.
It does not replace project-specific security rule testing or production review.
It focuses on common Firebase patterns, not every Google Cloud service.
It may need companion skills for payments, email delivery, advanced OAuth, relational databases, and search.

use_cases.title: Plan a Firestore schema
use_cases.description: Design query-first collections, denormalized documents, and cost-aware listeners before building a product feature.

use_cases.title: Review security rules
use_cases.description: Check ownership, admin, public profile, and private subcollection rules before publishing sensitive data.

use_cases.title: Implement Firebase auth
use_cases.description: Add social login, account linking, session persistence, email verification, password resets, and backend token checks.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Firebase app
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Firebase app for [product]. Recommend Firebase services, basic collections, auth needs, and local emulator setup.

prompt_templates.title: Model Firestore data
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Firestore data model for [feature]. Include query patterns, document structure, denormalized fields, indexes, and read cost concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Write security rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft Firestore security rules for [collections]. Include owner checks, admin checks, validation rules, and rule test cases I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Plan production Firebase architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Firebase architecture for [application]. Evaluate Auth, Firestore, Cloud Functions, Storage, Hosting, emulator tests, cost risks, and migration limits.

output_examples.input: I need comments, likes, and profiles in Firestore.
output_examples.output: A query-first schema plan with collections, embedded public author fields, subcollections, required indexes, and listener cost notes.

output_examples.input: I want Firebase Auth with a custom backend API.
output_examples.output: A token flow that gets an ID token, verifies it in Cloud Functions, handles expired tokens, and returns clear 401 responses.

output_examples.input: My rules allow public profiles but private settings.
output_examples.output: A rule review that separates public and private documents, checks owner writes, restricts admin collections, and lists emulator tests.

best_practices: Design collections around the queries the app must run most often.
Test security rules with the Firebase Emulator Suite before production changes.
Use Cloud Functions for privileged work that clients should never perform.
anti_patterns: Do not copy relational database models directly into Firestore.
Do not use broad public reads or writes for convenience during development.
Do not keep real-time listeners open when a view no longer needs them.

faq.question: Does this skill cover Firestore security rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes ownership, admin, public profile, and private subcollection patterns, plus guidance to test rules locally.

faq.question: Can it build a complete Firebase app?
faq.answer: It helps design and implement common Firebase patterns, but it does not run deployments or connect to your Firebase account.

faq.question: Does it include Firebase Auth?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers social login, redirect flows, account linking, session persistence, email verification, password reset, and ID token handling.

faq.question: Can I use it with React, Vue, or Angular?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists ReactFire, VueFire, and AngularFire as framework options, with general patterns that also work outside those libraries.

faq.question: Does it help reduce Firebase costs?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes query-first modeling, denormalization, listener cleanup, batch limits, and read cost planning.

faq.question: When should I avoid Firebase?
faq.answer: Avoid it for strongly relational workloads, complex joins, or heavy full-text search unless you add a specialized service.
